structured_output.hypothesis: Among native (non-introduced, non-domesticated) terrestrial, non-volant mammal species, essentially none have natural ranges confined to islands lying more than ~300 miles (~480 km) from any continent or large continental island.
structured_output.pass_criterion: After excluding bats, marine mammals and species with Holocene/historical human-mediated introduction, and treating Darwin's "great continental island" as islands of at least ~100,000 km2 (e.g., New Guinea, Borneo, Madagascar, Britain, Japan main islands, Sumatra, Cuba, Hispaniola), at most 3 native terrestrial species (<0.1% of non-volant terrestrial species) have natural ranges wholly on islands with nearest-landmass distance greater than 480 km. Such cases are reviewed manually and counted only if not extinct-by-introduction artefacts.
structured_output.fail_criterion: More than 10 native terrestrial non-volant mammal species (or more than 5 distinct islands or island groups) have natural ranges wholly on islands more than 480 km from the nearest continent or large continental island, after manual verification of nativity (e.g., Galapagos rice rats, Canary Islands shrew/giant rats, Philippine/Wallacean endemics beyond the threshold, Hawaii, New Zealand, etc.). A count between 4 and 10 is inconclusive.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's "terrestrial mammal" is interpreted as any non-volant, non-marine mammal, so bats are excluded as he did. "Native" corresponds to PHYLACINE's present natural range, which models ranges as if no human impact, so introductions and domesticates are excluded by design. "Island more than 300 miles from a continent or great continental island" is computed as great-circle distance greater than 483 km from the island's coast to the nearest continental landmass or large continental island, using a global landmass polygon layer such as Natural Earth. The fields used are the 1-degree-grid present natural range rasters and Trait_data (Order, Family, Binomial, Terrestrial, Marine, and Island Endemicity). The data includes late Quaternary extinct species, so the test is run separately for extant-only and for extant-plus-extinct species, with the extant-only result as primary. Known modern counterexamples are expected to arise mainly from endemic rodents on oceanic islands (e.g., Galapagos, Canary Islands, Juan Fernandez), and New Zealand (only bats native) is a supporting case. This makes the claim likely falsified at the strict universal reading, but the test applies the author's stated scope.

dataset.why_it_fits: Open Zenodo record with a downloadable zip (PHYLACINE_v1.2.1.zip) of a global mammal database covering all extant and late Quaternary extinct mammals. As PHYLACINE is generally documented, it holds trait data and present natural range maps that estimate ranges without human impact, so island-restricted native species can be identified. These can be joined against a landmass layer to compute distance to the nearest continent or large continental island. The Zenodo page itself only lists the zip, so the contents must be confirmed on download.
